about: Projects of several files, results, tests and the limits of the language

rows.title: Known limits and what is planned — Behaviour limits
rows.summary: no `@override`, no N0106. Fix: generate the package with `tools/defs` and list it in `defs`.
body: - External classes not in the type definitions (third-party packages like provider) leave the module open:
no `@override`, no N0106. Fix: generate the package with `tools/defs` and list it in `defs`.
- Result only propagates through Nuclear functions with a Result return (see [result.md](result.md)).
- TypeScript/Node have no type definition packages yet.
- An enum field of a model gets `null` in generated tests, and so does a field with a converter whose type is
neither basic nor `DateTime`.
- The integration test needs a device (here `-d linux`, with CMake).

rows.title: Known limits and what is planned — Not expressible in Nuclear yet
rows.summary: works); operator overloading (`Offset.zero & size`); `const` inference in Dart.
body: - Dart 3 pattern `switch`; declaring named or `factory` constructors (`Character.fromJson`; calling them
works); operator overloading (`Offset.zero & size`); `const` inference in Dart.
- Patterns only in assignments (not in lambda parameters, `for` or `match` branches).
- Records: decided they do NOT exist (ADR-0031).

rows.summary: &dialects)` by the dialect's `[project] marker`).
body: - `Manifest` (`nuclear.toml`, or inferred: `Manifest::infer(root, dialect, out)`, `Manifest::find(path,
&dialects)` by the dialect's `[project] marker`).
- `build()`: pass 1 = declarations of every file (`Emitter::declarations`, `ProjectCtx`); pass 2 = emit each
file with that table. A name of another file is used without `use`: the import is written.
- `[architecture]` rules (the linter, ADR-0046): N0301 (callers, names), N0302 (component privacy), checked by
tokens inside each declaration. `scope`, `public`, `exempt`, `callers`, `names`. All are errors today.
- Result runtime in `nuclear/result`; `[project.files]` templates (`project_context`: `decls`, `kinds.<k>`,
`decorated.<d>`, `files`, `has.<kind>`, `has.@<decorator>`); a project file whose template renders empty is not
written; it imports the files whose names its code writes.
- `[project] sources/kinds/files/outputs/assets/marker/output`. Kind by folder (`[project.kinds]`). Assets: text
files go to `generated`, others to `ProjectOutput.copies` (path → source).
- `config.nuc` (ADR-0065): `[project.manifest] file, sections, packages, reserved`; `project::read_config`
(section → arguments as text, N0303), `check_config` (reserved/dialect packages → N0303),
`reserved_package`. `build` returns it in `out.files` with an empty `out_path` (writers skip empty paths).

rows.title: Result and aliases — Aliases (ADR-0037, base §4.1.2)
rows.summary: `f() = Module.method` with empty `()`, no return type, and `Module` of the file with that method.
body: `f() = Module.method` with empty `()`, no return type, and `Module` of the file with that method.
`alias::expand` (called in `lib.rs::transpile`, before the emitter) rewrites it in the AST as
`f(params of method) ret = Module().method(params)` (`~` if async, `yield ...` if generator, `Module.method` if
`static`; `{}` params passed by name). So `collect`, Result and async know nothing about aliases. A
constructor with required params → N0112.

rows.title: Result and aliases — Result<E, T> (ADR-0036, 0047, 0048; `spec/nuclear-base.md` §3.2)
rows.summary: Limits: Result only propagates through functions/methods written in Nuclear with a Result return (not external libraries nor methods of external bases); `~f().error(...)` on an async function does not chain (store it first in a variable typed `Result`).
body: Limits: Result only propagates through functions/methods written in Nuclear with a Result return (not
external libraries nor methods of external bases); `~f().error(...)` on an async function does not chain
(store it first in a variable typed `Result`).

rows.title: Result and aliases — Result<E, T> (ADR-0036, 0047, 0048; `spec/nuclear-base.md` §3.2)
rows.summary: Error first, like `Either`.
body: Error first, like `Either`. No parser or AST changes (`Ok(x) ->` already parsed as a value pattern). All of it
lives in `emit.rs`, section "Result":
- `result_info` knows which calls give a Result (functions/methods of the file with that return, via
`DeclInfo.sig`/`method_sigs`; variable types in `Frame.types`).
- `FnCtx` says whether the function returns Result (propagates) and whether its last line keeps it.
- `propagate` writes into `pending` the lines `const xResult = ...;` + `result_propagate`; `with_pending`
puts them before each statement. `hoist_blocked` forbids propagating in lazy branches (N0110).
- `keep_next` keeps a Result (typed variable, return, match subject, Result parameter).
- `.ok/.error` → templates `result_then/tap/recover/tap_error` per `callback_returns_result`.
- Runtime: optional template `result_runtime` (`dialects/typescript/templates/result.tpl`), written after the
imports if `uses_result`. Dart has none: fpdart (`[types] Result = "Either"`, `Right`/`Left` via
`[names] written` + `[auto_imports]`; `result_value` = `(r as Right<E, T>).value` with `result_types`).
- A file that declares Result/Ok/Err sets `result_builtin = false`. Diagnostics N0108–N0111.

rows.title: Lexer and parser — AST shape
rows.summary: `Decl.words` (kinds/modifiers before the name), clauses after it, `Decl.generic_bounds` (`<T: Comparable>`), `Call.type_args`, `ExprKind::{Spread, ListIf, Cascade, CascadeSelf}`, destructuring patterns.
body: `Decl.words` (kinds/modifiers before the name), clauses after it, `Decl.generic_bounds` (`<T: Comparable>`),
`Call.type_args`, `ExprKind::{Spread, ListIf, Cascade, CascadeSelf}`, destructuring patterns. `BinaryOp` has
`IntDiv Pow BitOr BitXor BitAnd Shl Shr UShr`, `UnaryOp::BitNot`, `AssignOp::{Rem, BitAnd, BitOr, BitXor, Shl,
Shr, UShr}` (ADR-0086). The LSP walks
the AST itself: changing variants breaks `crates/nuclear-lsp` and `dragonfly/`.

rows.title: Lexer and parser — Comments (ADR-0080)
rows.summary: A `//` at the start of a line continues on ` * ` lines (the `*` in the column of the second `/`); the text of each is what follows `* `.
body: A `//` at the start of a line continues on ` * ` lines (the `*` in the column of the second `/`); the text of
each is what follows `* `. A more indented line of another shape still belongs to the comment but is N0021,
with its fix. Trailing empty lines (a lone ` *`) are dropped. The comment right above a declaration is its
doc (`DocComment`, ADR-0079).

rows.title: Lexer and parser — Habits of other languages (ADR-0088)
rows.summary: `habits::scan` (called by `parse`) masks strings and comments, then looks at each line for forms of TypeScript, Dart, Python, Java and Go (`{ }` blocks, `await`, `const x =`, `new`, `class A extends B`, the return type first, `def`, trailing `:`, `elif`, `None`, `#`, `x++`, `import`...) and…
body: `habits::scan` (called by `parse`) masks strings and comments, then looks at each line for forms of TypeScript,
Dart, Python, Java and Go (`{ }` blocks, `await`, `const x =`, `new`, `class A extends B`, the return type first,
`def`, trailing `:`, `elif`, `None`, `#`, `x++`, `import`...) and reports N0022 with a fix when it is exact. `parse`
drops the other diagnostics of those lines. A false positive is a bug: every `.nuc` of the repository and every
`nuclear` block of the docs must give none (checked by hand when the rules change; tests in `habits.rs`).

rows.title: Lexer and parser — Indentation
rows.summary: The lexer emits INDENT/DEDENT so the parser works as if there were braces.
body: The lexer emits INDENT/DEDENT so the parser works as if there were braces. Inside `()[]{}` indentation is
ignored, except for a lambda block: after `=>` + newline, or after `(params)` (a `(` after `=`, `(`, `[` or
`,`) + a more indented line. The block ends when the indentation returns to its first line; the lexer
synthesizes the `,` if missing. A `.method()` line less indented than the open block closes it and continues
the chain (parser: `chain_after_block`).

rows.title: Lexer and parser — Punctuation details
rows.summary: `List<List<int>>` still closes two generics.
body: - `!` right after a name/`)`/`]` is `Punct::Bang` (non-null); anywhere else it is N0009 (use `not`).
- The `<` of a generic call must touch the name (`call_type_args`); with a space it is a comparison.
- `>>`, `>>>`, `>>=`, `>>>=` are NOT tokens: the parser joins `>` tokens written together (`glued_gt`), so
`List<List<int>>` still closes two generics. `<<`, `<<=`, `**`, `~/`, `&`, `^`, `%=`, `&=`, `|=`, `^=` are tokens
- `r"..."` (an `r` touching a quote) is raw text: no escapes, no interpolation (`raw_string`). Numbers: `0b1010`
(`NumberKind::Bin`), exponents `1.5e-3` (Float).
- `..` with `nl_before` is a cascade, not a range. The parser does not open cascades inside a section
(`in_cascade`); a `.` line below a section continues that section (as in Dart).

rows.title: Multi-file projects — 1.1 The project card: `.nuclear/project.json`
rows.summary: Next to the card, the same commands write `.nuclear/map.md`, the project map: every declaration of the project grouped by component, with its kind, its description (its doc comment) and its members, in Nuclear (aliases as `list() = ListTasks.exec`, decorators as written).
body: Next to the card, the same commands write `.nuclear/map.md`, the **project map**: every declaration of the project
grouped by component, with its kind, its description (its doc comment) and its members, in Nuclear (aliases as
`list() = ListTasks.exec`, decorators as written). It is what an agent reads before it writes — the business of each
component without opening every file — and it is the same for every dialect of the platform.

rows.title: Multi-file projects — 1.1 The project card: `.nuclear/project.json`
rows.summary: Every tool that builds a project (`nuclear build`, `nuclear check`, `dragonfly build`, the editors when a file of the project is opened or saved) writes `.nuclear/project.json`, the card of the project: what it is, for an editor client or a script that must not read Nuclear or load the dialect.
body: Every tool that builds a project (`nuclear build`, `nuclear check`, `dragonfly build`, the editors when a file of the
project is opened or saved) writes `.nuclear/project.json`, the card of the project: what it is, for an editor
client or a script that must not read Nuclear or load the dialect. It is derived from the manifest and the dialect
(never edited by hand; rewritten when it changes):
```json
"name": "tasks_api",
"platform": "backend",
"dialect": "fastapi",
"language": "python",
"output": "build",
"plugins": ["sqlite", "ollama"],
"kinds": { "controller": "platform:backend", "data": "language:python", "jobs": "package:jobs 1.2.0" },
"toolchain": { "url": "http://localhost:8000", "serve": null, "installed": ".venv" }
`toolchain` copies three keys of the dialect's `[toolchain]` (spec/dialects.md): where the running app answers, the
command an editor runs to serve it itself, and the folder whose presence means the dependencies are installed.
`platform` is `null` for a project of a language dialect. `kinds` lists every kind the project can use with its
source (ADR-0095): the language dialect, the platform's contract or a kind package. The editors read it for the
status bar; the language server itself reads the manifest (`config.nuc` or `nuclear.toml`) and checks each project
with its own dialect, whatever the editor's default dialect is.

rows.title: Multi-file projects — 1.2 The contract: `.nuclear/contract.json` and `contracts(...)`
rows.summary: Every build writes `contracts/<name>/` from the contract: `models/<model>.nuc` for each model a route carries, `models/<name>_error.nuc` (`<Name>Error`, the error every call answers with) and one `repository` per controller with a method per route (`{id}` → `:id`; `@path`/`@query`/`@body` when a…
body: Every build writes `contracts/<name>/` from the contract: `models/<model>.nuc` for each model a route carries,
`models/<name>_error.nuc` (`<Name>Error`, the error every call answers with) and one `repository` per controller
with a method per route (`{id}` → `:id`; `@path`/`@query`/`@body` when a parameter is not where the verb would put
it; `Result<<Name>Error, T>`; the backend's doc comments). Only decorators the client's dialect consumes are written
(`@primary` and the validation rules where they exist; a GET that answers a keyed model gets `local = true` where
the local database exists). The files say they are generated and are rewritten on every build (a path contract) or
by `nuclear contracts update` (a url contract, which keeps a copy in `contracts/<name>/contract.json`: commit it, a
build never needs the network). A contract that cannot be read is `N0307`; a field the backend renamed is unknown
in the client at its next build (`N0116`).
```sh
nuclear contracts list            # each contract, its source and the version of the local copy
nuclear contracts update [name]   # fetch (url) or read (path) and regenerate contracts/<name>/
Example: `examples/examples-flutter-dialect/tasks_app` over `examples/examples-backend/tasks_api`.

rows.title: Multi-file projects — 1.2 The contract: `.nuclear/contract.json` and `contracts(...)`
rows.summary: The same call also writes `.nuclear/contract.json` (ADR-0098): what the project exposes or calls, in Nuclear's notation, the same whatever the dialect.
body: The same call also writes `.nuclear/contract.json` (ADR-0098): what the project exposes or calls, in Nuclear's
notation, the same whatever the dialect. A backend lists its `controllers` (path, routes with verb, path, parameters
and where each goes: `path`, `query` or `body`, the answer and error types, the status) and a mobile or web app its
`repositories` (the calls it makes); both list the `models` those carry (fields with type, `optional`, `default`,
`json` name, `rules` such as `minLength`, the `key` field, doc comments as `description`). A backend also gets
`.nuclear/openapi.json` (OpenAPI 3.1 from the contract); both files are copied into the output folder and the
runtimes serve them at `GET /.nuclear/contract.json` and `GET /.nuclear/openapi.json`.
A client declares the backends it talks to in its manifest, with the name of the connection its calls use:
```nuclear
dragonfly(platform = "mobile", dialect = "flutter")
app(name = "tasks_app", version = "1.0.0+1")
contracts(tasks_api = "../tasks_api")              // a backend built next to this project (its .nuclear/contract.json)
contracts(tasks_api = "https://api.example.com")   // or the running API: nuclear contracts update fetches it

rows.title: Multi-file projects — 1. Manifest
rows.summary: A Dragonfly project (a platform of ADR-0093) has only `.nuc` files; its manifest is `config.nuc`: // config.nuc dragonfly(platform = "backend", dialect = "fastapi") // the platform written, the dialect it is built with app(name = "tasks_api", description = "Tasks and an assistant.", version =…
body: A Dragonfly project (a platform of ADR-0093) has only `.nuc` files; its manifest is `config.nuc`:
```nuclear
// config.nuc
dragonfly(platform = "backend", dialect = "fastapi")   // the platform written, the dialect it is built with
app(name = "tasks_api", description = "Tasks and an assistant.", version = "0.1.0")
plugins(sqlite = true, ollama = true)                   // §3.3
`dragonfly(...)` is required: `platform` is `web`, `mobile` or `backend`; `dialect` one of the platform's dialects
(N0303 otherwise). `app(...)` names the generated package (`name`, in snake_case) and its description and
version; `title` is the app's name as people read it (`title = "NuclearLang"`: the window or tab title; the name
when absent); a platform may take more fields (`usesMaterialDesign` in mobile). The output folder is the dialect's
(`[project] output`, §3). Changing `dialect` changes nothing else in the project.
A project of a language dialect without Dragonfly uses `nuclear.toml`:

rows.title: Multi-file projects — 1. Manifest
rows.summary: nuclear build <folder> # transpiles the project into <folder>/<out> nuclear build <folder> -o <output> # into another folder nuclear check <folder> [--json] # only the errors of every file An error in any file stops writing: nothing is written.
body: ```sh
nuclear build <folder>               # transpiles the project into <folder>/<out>
nuclear build <folder> -o <output>   # into another folder
nuclear check <folder> [--json]      # only the errors of every file
An error in any file stops writing: nothing is written.
`nuclear.toml` is optional when the dialect declares a file that marks its projects (`[project] marker`, §3):
the folder that has it is a project of that dialect, its name is the folder's (in snake_case) unless `app(name)`
says otherwise, and its output, `[project] output`. Every Dragonfly dialect marks its projects with `config.nuc`,
whose `dragonfly(...)` names the dialect (§3.1).

rows.title: Multi-file projects — 2. Files and names
rows.summary: `[project] sources = "lib"` in the dialect, `components/users/data/user_repository.nuc` → `lib/components/users/data/user_repository.dart`.
body: - Each `x.nuc` is written to `<sources>/x.<extension>` with the same relative path: with
`[project] sources = "lib"` in the dialect, `components/users/data/user_repository.nuc` →
`lib/components/users/data/user_repository.dart`.
- Hidden folders and the output folder are not read.
- A name is declared only once in the whole project (`N0303`).
- Every name declared in a file can be used in the others without `use`: the transpiler writes the import
of the file that declares it. The dialect's `project_import` template gives the import path (Dart:
`package:{{project}}/{{path}}.dart`; Python: `{{package}}.{{path}}`, where `package` is the folder the files go
to: the manifest's `package`, else the dialect's `sources`).
- A file is imported only if the generated code uses one of its names (comments and the text of strings do
not count; their interpolations do).
- What holds for the declarations of one file holds across files: `Result` propagation, aliases
(`f() = Module.method` with `Module` in another file), overrides of bases in another file and named
arguments.
- The `Result` runtime is written once, in `<sources>/nuclear/result.<extension>`, and the files that use
it import it (if the dialect has its own runtime; Dart uses fpdart).
- `main` (the entry point) is never imported from another file.

rows.title: Multi-file projects — 3.1 Manifest in Nuclear: `[project.manifest]`
rows.summary: The file has only top-level calls to those sections, with named arguments whose value is a string, a number or a boolean (`dependencies(hive = "^2.2.3")`).
body: The file has only top-level calls to those sections, with named arguments whose value is a string, a
number or a boolean (`dependencies(hive = "^2.2.3")`). It is checked with the project (another section, an
unnamed argument or a value that is not a literal is `N0303`) and it is not transpiled: it has no output
(empty `out_path`). The framework's CLI reads it with `project::read_config` (section → arguments as text)
to write the target's manifest (the `pubspec.yaml` in Flutter).
A `packages` section only lists third-party packages the framework does not use: a package of the dialect
(its `defs`, not the ones the project added) or of `reserved` is `N0303` on its line
(`project::check_config`, `project::reserved_package`).

rows.title: Multi-file projects — 3.1 Manifest in Nuclear: `[project.manifest]`
rows.summary: A backend dialect has the `dependencies` section too (`dependencies(nuclear_graph = ">=0.1")`): each package goes to the generated manifest (`pyproject.toml`, `package.json`) as the template variable `dependencies` (`name`, `version`, `path`); a version that starts with `.` or `/` is a folder on…
body: A backend dialect has the `dependencies` section too (`dependencies(nuclear_graph = ">=0.1")`): each package goes to
the generated manifest (`pyproject.toml`, `package.json`) as the template variable `dependencies` (`name`,
`version`, `path`); a version that starts with `.` or `/` is a folder on disk, resolved from the project root
(`nuclear_graph @ file:///...`, `"file:/..."`).

rows.title: Multi-file projects — 3.2 Type definitions of the project: `build/defs.lock` and `defs/`
rows.summary: The packages a project adds (besides the dialect's `defs`) are listed in `build/defs.lock`, one per line (`hive@2.2.3`), or kept in the project itself under `defs/<language>/<name>/<version>/` (a package of the project's own code, or one no cache has).
body: The packages a project adds (besides the dialect's `defs`) are listed in `build/defs.lock`, one per line
(`hive@2.2.3`), or kept in the project itself under `defs/<language>/<name>/<version>/` (a package of the project's
own code, or one no cache has). The framework's CLI writes the lock: it resolves the versions and generates the
missing definitions into the cache (`~/.cache/nuclearlang/defs`, [definitions.md](definitions.md) §1). Every tool
that transpiles or checks the project (`nuclear build|check`, `dragonfly`, the LSP) adds both to the dialect with
`project::with_project_defs(root, dialect)` (`project_defs` lists them); a package that cannot be loaded is a
warning.
A kind by folder applies only to PascalCase declarations that are neither enums nor functions and carry no
other header word.
Variables of a `[project.files]` template:

rows.title: Multi-file projects — 3.2 Type definitions of the project: `build/defs.lock` and `defs/`
rows.summary: Each declaration of `decls` (and of `kinds.<kind>`) also brings `generics` (its type parameters: `name`), `fields` (`name`, `type`, `tinfo`, `optional`, `decor`) and `methods` (`name`, `owner`, `owner_decor`, `decor`, `deco_args`, `params_list`, `param_groups`, `ret_info`).
body: | Variable | Content |
| `project` | the manifest's `name` |
| `decls` | each declaration: `name`, `kind`, `component`, `path`, `import`, `params` (constructor parameters: `name`, `type`...), `decor` |
| `kinds.<kind>` | the declarations of that kind |
| `decorated.<decorator>` | the declarations with that decorator |
| `files` | one `import` per file whose names the generated code writes |
| `has.<kind>`, `has.@<decorator>` | the project has at least one declaration of that kind or with that decorator |
| `components` | each component (`name`) with its declarations by kind (`kinds.<kind>`): a framework module per component |
| `uses.<Name>` | the generated code of the project writes that name (`{{#uses.Postgres}}` asks for its driver) |
Each declaration of `decls` (and of `kinds.<kind>`) also brings `generics` (its type parameters: `name`),
`fields` (`name`, `type`, `tinfo`, `optional`, `decor`) and `methods` (`name`, `owner`, `owner_decor`,
`decor`, `deco_args`, `params_list`, `param_groups`, `ret_info`).

rows.title: Multi-file projects — 3.3 Plugins: `[project.plugins]` and `plugins(...)` in `config.nuc`
rows.summary: The plugin's type definitions are always loaded (their index only), so an editor still completes them.
body: - `plugins(...)` takes only plugins of the dialect, with `true` or `false` (N0303); `requires` enables the others.
- A kind, or a name of a plugin's `defs` or `names`, used without enabling it is **N0304**, with the line to add.
The plugin's type definitions are always loaded (their index only), so an editor still completes them.
- The templates of `[project.files]` get `plugins.<name>` (enabled), `plugins.packages` and `plugins.dev_packages`
(`name`, `version`, `local`): a `pyproject.toml` or `package.json` lists only the enabled packages, and a file
whose template renders nothing (`{{#plugins.genkit}}...{{/plugins.genkit}}`) is not written.
- A **kind package** of the platform (`kinds/<name>/`, [dialects.md](dialects.md) §7) is a plugin too: its `[plugin]`
table gives the packages, defs and names; its kinds are the kinds it defines. One without an implementation for
the project's dialect is N0306 when enabled.
- The framework's CLI adds the packages of the enabled plugins to the target's manifest and removes those of a
plugin turned off (Flutter: `dragonfly build`, `build/app/.dragonfly_plugins`). `project::enabled_plugins(root,
dialect)` gives the list.
Other variables of `[project.files]` templates: `components` (each component, `name`, with its declarations by kind:
`kinds.<kind>`) and `uses.<Name>` (the generated code writes that name).

rows.title: Multi-file projects — 3.3 Plugins: `[project.plugins]` and `plugins(...)` in `config.nuc`
rows.summary: A dialect lists the optional parts of its framework (Genkit, Kafka, LangChain, a database driver).
body: A dialect lists the optional parts of its framework (Genkit, Kafka, LangChain, a database driver). A project carries
a plugin only when its `config.nuc` enables it, so it never gets heavier than what it uses (ADR-0092):
```nuclear
// config.nuc
plugins(genkit = true, googleAI = true)

rows.title: Multi-file projects — 4. Architecture rules: `[architecture]`
rows.summary: The dialect declares which declarations may use others; the transpiler checks it across the whole project (it is the framework's linter):
body: The dialect declares which declarations may use others; the transpiler checks it across the whole project
(it is the framework's linter):
| Rule | Code |
| A declaration uses one of a `callers` kind without being of an allowed kind | `N0301` |
| A declaration with a kind uses a `names` name without being of an allowed kind | `N0301` |
| A declaration uses something of another component whose kind is not in `public` | `N0302` |

rows.title: Multi-file projects — 5. Data for kind templates
rows.summary: `[decorators]` of the dialect:
body: | Field | What it does |
| `async_methods = true` | all its methods are asynchronous (a `~` calls them) |
| `methods = ["exec"]` | the only allowed methods (`N0215`) |
| `returns = "Result"` | the type each method returns (`N0216`) |
| `file_header = "part '{{file}}.g.dart';"` | written once after the file's imports |
| `alias_via = "inject"` | an alias of the class takes the instance from that function: `inject<Module>().method(...)` |
| `declares = ["{{name}}Builder"]` | other classes the template writes: the program may use them |

| `provide = { template = "inject<{{name}}>()", kinds = ["usecase"] }` | inside the kind, a program declaration of those kinds is read with the template: `GetUser.exec()` → `inject<GetUser>().exec()` |
| `results = "keep"` | inside the kind, a `Result` never propagates: it is kept as a value (tests) |
| `void_methods = true` | its methods do not return their last line (tests) |
| `imports` | imported if the generated code writes that name |
`[decorators]` of the dialect:

rows.title: Multi-file projects — 5. Data for kind templates
rows.summary: Kind fields for frameworks:
body: | `ret_info`, `tinfo` | methods, functions, parameters | of the type: `type`, `list`, `item`, `name` (name in Nuclear, without type arguments), `args` (the type arguments, each with this same data: `Page<Character>`), `generic` (a type parameter of the declaration: `T`), `model` (a class of the program, or of the type definitions that reads itself from JSON: the runtime's `PageOf`), `runtime` (a `model` of the type definitions, not of the program), `fields_decor.<decorator>` and `decor` of a model (its first field with that decorator: `primary` → `id`; its own decorators: `decor.entity.arg`, the table), `primitive`, `void`, `nullable`, `is.<name>`; of a `Result<T, E>`: `result`, `full`, `err`, `err_is.<name>` and the rest describes `T` |
| `override` | `field` | the field replaces a member of a base |
| `file`, `project`, `component`, `kind` | kind | name of the file, the project, the component and the kind |
| `app.name`, `app.title`, `app.description`, `app.version` | project files | `app(...)` of `config.nuc` (`title`: the name when absent) |

| `asset.<path>` | project files | a file of the `[project] assets` folders exists, its path with `/`, `.` and `-` as `_` (`asset.public_styles_css`: index.html links the stylesheet only when the project has one) |
Kind fields for frameworks:

rows.title: Multi-file projects — 5. Data for kind templates
rows.summary: 5. Data for kind templates
body: | Variable | Where | Content |

| `decor` | kind, `method`, `method_signature`, `function`, `field`, parameters | each decorator → `arg` (first positional argument), `args` (all), `items` (elements of a list argument), `path` (a first text argument as a route: its `{x}` segments written as `[options] route_param` says, `":name"` for NestJS; `@get("{id}")` → `decor.get.path` = `:id`) and each named argument. A named argument that is a list also gives its `items` (`decor.screen.providers.items`), and one that is an object, each field (`decor.screen.loggedIn.forward`); `{{decor.screen.providers}}` is still its code |
| `deco_args` | kind, methods, functions | the named arguments of all its decorators together |
| `owner_decor` | methods, `constructor`, `field` | `decor` of the class |
| `owner` | methods, `field` | name of the class |
| `params_list` | kind, methods, functions | each parameter: `name`, `type`, `tinfo`, `optional`, `named`, `decor`, `decorated` |
| `param_groups` | methods | `plain` (no decorator) and one group per decorator (`path`, `query`), each `{ list }` |
| `call_args` | methods | the parameters as the arguments of a call (`id, name: name`) |

rows.title: Multi-file projects — 5. Data for kind templates
rows.summary: 5. Data for kind templates
body: | Key | What it does |
| `consumed` | decorators the templates read and that are not written to the target |

| `[decorators.provide]` | decorator (or `decorator.argument`) → template: with `"screen.providers" = "context.read<{{name}}>()"`, in a declaration with `@screen(providers = [Manager])`, `Manager.x()` is `context.read<Manager>().x()` |

| `[decorators.args]` | decorator → its named arguments: `["route", "loggedIn", "loggedIn.forward!"]` (`a.b` = field of object `a`; `!` = required). One that is not listed, or a required one that is missing, is `N0217` |
| `void` | a method with that decorator returns nothing to its caller |

body: A framework's kinds generate code from decorators and signatures. Besides the usual variables

rows.title: Multi-file projects
rows.summary: A project is a folder with a `nuclear.toml` manifest and `.nuc` files in any subfolder.
body: A **project** is a folder with a `nuclear.toml` manifest and `.nuc` files in any subfolder. It is
transpiled as a whole: each file sees the declarations of the others. This document describes the
mechanism, which is the same for every dialect; what each framework does with it is in its spec (for
example, the [flutter](https://github.com/nuclearlang/dragonfly-mobile/blob/main/spec/flutter.md) dialect).
